notes: 200 sentences for fine-tuning F5-TTS on Sonali Maitra's voice. Mix: ~50 Harvard sentences (public domain, phonetically balanced), ~50 general varied English, ~100 guided-imagery register sentences (second person, present tense, calm, sensory). Target: ~30-45 min of recording at a calm reading pace.

Let your eyes close, gently.
Take a slow breath in. And let it go.
Feel the weight of your body where it rests.
There is nowhere else you need to be, right now.
Just this breath. Just this one breath.
Notice the small sounds around you. The room. The quiet.
You don't have to do anything. You don't have to be anywhere.
Settle into the chair. Or the cushion. Wherever you are.
Let the day, for a moment, fall away from your shoulders.
Breathe in slowly. And out, even more slowly.
Imagine yourself, a year from now, sitting somewhere you love.
What does the light look like, in that room?
What are you wearing? How does the fabric feel against your skin?
Notice your breath. It is calmer than it usually is.
Notice the way you carry yourself, here. Look at your shoulders.
This version of you knows something the present-day you is still learning.
Let yourself feel the satisfaction of it. The quiet kind. The earned kind.
There is no rush. We have all the time you need.
Picture someone you love walking into the room.
Notice how they look at you. Notice what they see.
You did the work. You walked the long road. You are here.
Stay with the feeling. Let it settle into your chest.
Notice the small things. The cup in your hand. The light through the window.
Your breath is slow. Your shoulders are soft. Your face is at rest.
Let the future-self look back, for a moment, at the present-day you.
What do you most want them to know?
Let the answer come, in its own time. There is no hurry.
Maybe it is one word. Maybe it is a feeling. Maybe it is the way your hands settle in your lap.
Whatever comes, let yourself receive it.
And now, slowly, begin to come back.
Notice the room around you again. The chair beneath you. The floor under your feet.
Carry something back with you. A feeling, an image, a quiet certainty.
Notice the breath again. Slow. Steady. Yours.
When you are ready — and only when you are ready — let your eyes open.
Welcome back.
Place your hand on your chest, just for a moment, and feel the rise and fall.
Notice where you are holding tension. Maybe the jaw. Maybe the shoulders. Maybe behind the eyes.
On the next exhale, let it soften.
There is nothing to fix. There is nothing to solve. Only this.
Picture a quiet morning. A morning you have not yet lived.
The light is soft. The air is cool. The day has not yet asked anything of you.
You are holding a warm cup in both hands.
You feel, with surprising clarity, that everything is going to be all right.
Let yourself believe it. Just for the length of this breath.
And another breath. And another.
Imagine a place that has always made you feel safe.
It may be real. It may be invented. It may be a place you have not yet been.
Look around. Take in what is there. The colors. The textures. The smell of the air.
You are welcome here. You have always been welcome here.
Sit, or stand, or lie down — whatever feels right.
Imagine someone you trust completely, walking up to where you are.
They are not in a hurry. They have come to be with you.
They sit beside you, and the silence between you feels like comfort.
There is no question they need answered. There is no problem they have come to solve.
They are simply here, with you, and that is enough.
What is one thing you want them to know?
Say it, silently, in your mind. Whenever you are ready.
Notice how they receive it. Notice the way their face softens.
And now, picture the version of you who is on the other side of what you are working on.
They are here, in this safe place, sitting across from you.
Look at them carefully. Look at their eyes. Look at the way they hold themselves.
Notice what is different. Notice what is the same.
Notice what they are no longer carrying, that you are carrying right now.
Ask them, gently: what helped most?
Listen. Don't argue with the answer. Just listen.
Maybe the answer comes in words. Maybe in an image. Maybe just in a feeling you cannot name.
However it comes, let it land.
Stay with it for a few breaths.
Now, slowly, let the image begin to dissolve.
The room around you returns. The chair. The floor. The light at the edges of your closed eyes.
Wiggle your fingers a little. Your toes.
Take one slow, deep breath in.
Let it go, all the way out.
And when you are ready, let your eyes open. Take your time.
Notice the room. The actual room you are in.
Notice what is the same. The wall. The light. The familiar shapes of your life.
And notice that you are, in some small way, different than when you closed your eyes.
Carry that with you. The way you might carry a stone in your pocket.
It is enough, for now, to know it is there.
Thank you. For showing up, and doing the work of imagining.
There is no right way to feel after this. Whatever you feel is what you feel.
And whatever else the day asks of you — you can meet it, one breath at a time.
Notice the sound of your own breath. It has been there the whole time.
It will be there, too, for the next part of your day. And the next. And the next.
You can come back to this, any time. The door is not locked.
Soften the corners of your mouth. Soften the muscles behind your eyes.
Let your tongue rest, gently, against the roof of your mouth.
Feel the chair, or the bed, or the floor, fully supporting you. You do not have to hold yourself up.
And now, more deeply — let go.
Imagine that today, you are exactly where you need to be.
Imagine that this hour — this very hour — was waiting for you to arrive in it.
Picture yourself, six months from now, walking through a place you love.
What season is it? What is the temperature of the air? What sounds do you hear?
Picture yourself, five years from now, sitting across from someone you love.
What are you talking about? What are you laughing about?
Picture yourself, ten years from now, standing in a doorway, looking back at a room.
What is in the room? What did you build, in those ten years, that is in this room?
Stay with whatever image came, however quiet, however brief.
It does not have to be clear. It only has to be true.
And now, gently, come back. We will return here again.
